shippingNews.postTitle: McCarthy Takes Final Coal Load from SMET Dock

stories.body: Walter J. McCarthy Jr. loading the last coal cargo at SMET on Saturday as Mesabi Miner backs toward the ore dock. [Scott Bjorklund] SUPERIOR, WI – The final vessel has departed with coal from the Midwest Energy Terminal in Superior, bringing a half-century of major fossil fuel transshipment on the Twin Ports waterfront to an official close. On Friday night, the 1,000-foot bulk carrier Walter J. McCarthy Jr. passed beneath the Duluth Aerial Lift Bridge to take on the terminal's concluding cargo before operations cease permanently. shippingNews.postTitle: Bulk Carrier Hits Docked Tanker at Montreal

stories.body: MONTREAL, QC – The bulk carrier Federal Beaufort arriving at the Port of Montreal Friday afternoon from downstream, reportedly struck the tanker Hinch Spirit, which was stationary and moored alongside at Section 35 while receiving bunkers. The Hinch Spirit reportedly sustained damage to her port quarter and starboard side, while the Federal Beaufort sustained damage to her bow. No injuries have been reported. Both vessels are currently moored alongside, awaiting divers and an investigation by Transport Canada. Janey Anderson – Ship Junkies - Lakes, Locks & Rivers (LL&R)

stories.body: DETROIT, MI – The oceanographic research vessel Neil Armstrong stopped in Detroit Friday to fuel. By 9 p.m. she was headed upriver and will pass Port Huron in the dark. todayInHistory.title: Fire Causes Significant Damage to Two Harbors Lighthouse Gift Shop
todayInHistory.text: TWO HARBORS, MN – An investigation is underway after a detached building that’s used as a gift shop for the Two Harbors Lighthouse went up in flames Monday evening. As of Tuesday morning, local authorities have yet to release information on the blaze, which likely broke out around 5:30 p.m. Officials with the Lake County Historical Society, which controls the lakeside property, told Northern News Now that no one was injured, but the damage to the building is significant. “We were literally watching a piece of Lake County’s history go up in those flames,” Lake County Historical Society Vice President David Johnson said in an interview with the station. It’s believed that the fire started in the breezeway between the gift shop and a connected structure, both of which are separate from the historic lighthouse. The Lake County Historical Society shared this statement: “We are incredibly grateful to the firefighters and first responders who have responded and are working to address the situation. Their time, dedication, and efforts are greatly appreciated.” Bring Me The News Gift shop fire at Two Harbors Lighthouse.

marineWeather.synopsis: 30.0 inch ridging lingers over Lake Superior this morning. Then a 29.6 inch low near Lake Winnipeg weakens to 29.7 inches as it traverses just north of Lake Superior this evening into tonight, sending a 29.8 inch trough across the lake. Weak 30.0 inch ridging returns on Tuesday before a 29.9 inch trough drops southeast over the lake Tuesday night and Wednesday. Then 30.4 inch high pressure over northern Manitoba gradually shifts south-southeast through Saturday, becoming centered over the lake at 30.3 inches on Saturday.

Winds will become southwesterly and increase through this evening as an area of low pressure around 29.7 inches progresses through the northern Canadian Prairies into northern Ontario. Winds become northwesterly behind the associated cold front early Tuesday morning, then diminish as high pressure around 30.1 inches builds into the central Plains and Mississippi River Valley. Low pressure crossing Illinois on Wednesday will strengthen to around 29.5 inches as it crosses Indiana early Thursday morning. An additional strengthening of the pressure gradient is expected over Lake Michigan on Thursday. This will bring breezy north- northeast winds Wednesday night through Thursday night. There is increasing potential for gales on Thursday and Thursday night, particularly over the southern two thirds of the lake. Wednesday night through Friday night, a strong north-to-south band of lake effect showers is expected to develop. It will be predominantly rain, though some snow could mix in at times. North winds remain gusty Friday, backing northwest and decelerating into Saturday.

Low pressure, 29.50 inches, over western Quebec and its cold front exit the central Great Lakes early this morning. Expect a few additional showers at times, mainly over Lake Huron. The pattern quickly shifts as high pressure briefly builds in today. Troughing returns Tuesday as the next clipper brushes the northern shores of Lake Superior, with its attendant cold front passing through. Note that the frontal passage is expected to be mainly dry. High pressure then returns Tuesday night into Wednesday.

High pressure 30.00 inches briefly builds into the region today. Low pressure 29.70 inches will move north of Lake Erie while dragging a cold front east across the lake early Tuesday. Another cold front crosses the lake Wednesday night into Thursday as low pressure 29.80 inches tracks south of the lake across the Ohio Valley.

A 29.4 inch low over the Canadian Maritimes today will move north to northern Quebec by late Tuesday. Meanwhile, another 29.7 inch low will move from northwest Ontario province tonight to southern Quebec Tuesday before reaching the Gulf of Maine by Wednesday. Another 29.5 inch low will develop over the Ohio Valley Wednesday night through Thursday, then give way to a secondary low along the Mid Atlantic coast by Thursday night. This 29.2 inch coastal low will move northeast along or offshore of the New England coast Friday through Saturday.
